key_insight: KnowBench reframes clinical AI evaluation around Effort Reduction (ER): how much system-generated work a clinician can accept after review, rather than how similar outputs look to a reference.
clinical_relevance: This approach is designed to measure real deployment impact across clinical documentation and workflow tasks, making it more relevant to administrative burden reduction in practice.
method: Defines ER as the proportion of AI-generated clinical work product accepted by the responsible clinician after expert and safety review.
Applies the same ER construction across multiple tasks, including notes, coding, orders, chart summaries, patient instructions, and decision support.
Uses clinician review-and-attestation as the ground truth, with corrections counted as residual effort returned to the clinician.
evidence_signal: In the documentation use case, the authors report over one million signed encounters across more than six months and 13 specialties, with an aggregate ER of 97.99% and per-specialty ER of 96.8%–98.9%.
watch_item: The release states that the reporting protocol is only partially checklist-complete and that some companion statistics are withheld, which limits full independent auditing.
paper_title: KnowBench: Effort Reduction as a Unified, Deployment-Grounded Benchmark for Clinical AI
